summary: Started the full dev stack via `pnpm dev:server:start`, verified agent server (8787) and Vite (5173, bound to IPv6 ::1) are reachable, then investigated why closing a browser tab aborts streaming sessions — traced to `attachAgentConnection` creating a fresh `PiAgentService`, `ProjectServiceRegistry`, and `ExtensionHostService` per WebSocket, all disposed on disconnect.
decisions: Use the existing `scripts/dev-server.ts` (via `pnpm dev:server:start/status/stop`) as the canonical way to run the dev stack in the background, rather than ad-hoc pnpm scripts.

Diagnosed that sessions-per-connection is the wrong ownership model for a single-user local app: closing a tab aborts streaming runs, two tabs can't share session events, and N extension hosts run for one user.

Proposed target model: one server-lifetime `PiAgentService` + `ProjectServiceRegistry` + `ExtensionHostService` created in `server.ts`, with connections as subscribers (attach/detach) to the shared `AgentEventHub`; per-connection factories retained only as test seams. Implementation not yet performed.
errors: Initial port check via git-bash `/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/5173` reported DOWN even after Vite logged 'ready'; root cause was Vite binding to IPv6 ::1 only, so 127.0.0.1 refused while ::1 accepted. Confirmed with a Node net check against `::1`.
`pnpm dev:server:status` exited non-zero with 'Gizmo Pi Web is not running' on the first call before the server was started (expected — server had not been launched yet).
